title: Tanzanian Boiled Groundnuts
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Karanga za Kuchemsha — fresh raw groundnuts boiled in their shells in heavily salted water until completely tender. The harvest season snack — softer, moister, and more complex than roasted peanuts. Sold at rainy season markets when fresh peanuts are available.
longDesc: Boiled groundnuts are the harvest season alternative to roasted — when fresh green peanuts are available immediately after the harvest, they are boiled in heavily salted water. The result is completely different from roasted peanuts: soft, moist, creamy, and mild. A seasonal treat that roasted peanuts cannot replicate.
steps: Place in a large pot. Cover with water by 5cm.
Add salt generously — the water should taste very salty.
Bring to a boil. Simmer covered for 40—50 minutes.
Test one — the nut inside should be completely soft and creamy.
Eat by cracking the shell and extracting the soft nut.
chefTips: The water must be genuinely salty — this seasons the nut through the shell.
Fresh green peanuts only — dried peanuts do not boil the same way.
commonMistakes: Under-boiling — nuts should be creamy soft.
cookingScience: Salt penetrates the peanut shell through osmosis during boiling — seasoning the nut from the outside in. This is why boiled peanuts are more uniformly seasoned than salted roasted peanuts. The soft texture results from starch gelatinisation at 100°C, which the hard structure of raw peanuts prevents.
sustainabilityTips: Seasonal harvest product — eaten when available, zero preservation needed.
culturalNote: Boiled groundnuts are the taste of harvest season in Tanzania — the brief annual window when fresh peanuts from the fields are available, transformed by salt and water into a completely different snack from the roasted version everyone knows year-round.
